title: Balanced scalar comparison for point sections
statement: For a field $k$, commutative ring sheaves $B,B\prime$ on the small pro-etale site of $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a:B\to B\prime$, and normalized tensor models $T,T\prime$ [def-sf-point-evaluation-tensor-data], define normalized scalar data to comprise a natural chain isomorphism $\kappa:\Gamma_s\circ a^*\cong(R\prime\otimes_R-)\circ\Gamma_s$, whose value on the actual sheafification-unit generator $b\otimes x$ is the ordinary tensor $b\otimes x$, and the ordinary coefficient tensor comparison $\epsilon$. Its inverse on every total summand is $(c\otimes x)\otimes(d\otimes y)\mapsto cd\otimes(x\otimes y)$. Here $R=B(s)$, $R\prime=B\prime(s)$, the scalar homomorphism is exactly $a_s$, and sheaf scalar extension is the canonical sheafified tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Mathlib places coefficients first; this is the balanced rule in that convention.

source.place: Tags 07A4 and 03EL; normalized point specialization in the Kunneth proof
